description:
Problem: .github/workflows/oracle-review.yml still runs the full checker on pull_request (opened, synchronize, reopened, edited, ready_for_review), pull_request_review (submitted, dismissed) and workflow_dispatch, and posts an oracle-review check run. On 2026-10-24 it ran 400+ times in about a day with about 48% failures: red X marks on pull requests for a check that no longer gates anything, on the same runners as the oracle. Since PR #3395 (43a3e5e60) and the ruleset edit of 2026-10-25T01:53Z, the App-bound oracle-gate is the only required oracle check. oracle-gate.yml still needs workflow_run completions of the workflow named oracle-review as its only trusted bridge for review events, because pull_request_review runs the pull request's own workflow file and cannot post the gate. oracle-verdict.yml also reruns failed oracle-review runs after posting (step 'Rerun the failed synchronize suite for this head', lines 1002-1011); it is the only user of the post job's actions: write permission (lines 900-902).

Outcome: oracle-review.yml keeps its file path and workflow name 'oracle-review'. It triggers only on pull_request_review [submitted, edited, dismissed]. It has permissions {} and one job with a distinct name (review-event): no checkout, no secrets, no API calls, one no-op step. No check run named oracle-review is produced. oracle-verdict.yml no longer lists or reruns oracle-review runs, and the post job's actions: write, used only by that step, is removed. oracle-gate.yml is not changed. The only change allowed in _project/scripts/oracle_gate.py is the argparse description string in _parse_args, which still describes the decision as the one 'the oracle-review check reads'.

Decision gates (stop and report if one fails):
1. Re-read oracle-gate.yml on current develop. Its workflow_run still lists oracle-review, and the bridge job still resolves the develop pull request by head SHA. If not, re-plan.
2. Read the live ruleset 15611785 and record a timestamped readback in context: oracle-review is absent, and oracle-gate is required with integration_id 5201041. If oracle-review is still required, stop: removing the producer would block every pull request.
3. Grep for every consumer of the oracle-review check name or of this workflow's jobs (scripts, _project/scripts, .github, tests, docs, .claude/skills). Update each consumer here or list it with a reason. scripts/check_comment_cleanup_scope.py belongs to comment-policy-oracle-gate-evidence-only-20261025; do not make it accept the new job.
4. Record the decision on 'edited'. Include it unless evidence shows that an edited review cannot change an oracle-gate input. The gate reads the current review body, so an edited oracle review can change the decision.

Item guardrails: do not rename the workflow or its file. Do not add pull_request or pull_request_target triggers. Do not name any job oracle-review. No checkout, secrets or token use in this workflow. Do not touch oracle-gate.yml, decide() in _project/scripts/oracle_review_check.py, or anything in oracle_gate.py except the _parse_args description string. Keep the release-tree exclusion of the workflow. The rewritten workflow test must not newly depend on files that release-cut removes. Do not add oracle-author filtering as a runner-cost optimization: skipping the notification job does not prevent the downstream bridge run.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, after make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. No SKIP or --no-verify, no stand-in approvals, no ruleset edits or bypasses, no raw gh pr merge. Close out with make pr-preflight, make pr-open, oracle SHIP on the exact head, then make pr-arm. Do not change oracle-gate's App binding (integration 5201041), the oracle decision rule, or the native review-thread-resolution requirement; oracle-gate stays the only required oracle check. Do not close and reopen, mass-rerun or rebase other pull requests. No explanatory comments or docstrings (COMMENT-POLICY-001). Every behavior change gets a test that fails on the previous code.
